title: Preserve zero-density tails in mixture log reductions
body:
## Problem

The manual max-shift in logsum_rows subtracts -inf from -inf when every component has zero representable density. This turns a valid log likelihood of -inf into NaN. Positive-infinity rows have the same invalid subtraction. With ordinary mixture sigmas of 1 or 2, a finite far-tail sample such as 1e155 already reaches the first case; the normalization coefficients themselves remain finite.

## Change

Use scipy.special.logsumexp along the existing row axis. SciPy is already a required dependency. Finite rows, sample shape, and the surrounding mixture/TPE formulas are preserved, while extended-real rows retain their correct results.

## Validation

- Seven new regressions: upstream base 6 failed, 1 passed.
- Fixed regressions plus the existing Gaussian and lognormal mixture math tests: 11 passed.
- Explicit row-sum references cover zero/infinite mass, finite values, and an empty sample batch.
- Gaussian-mixture tails are checked against independent SciPy normal log densities reduced with NumPy logaddexp.
- Native fmin/TPE/Trials runs continue from finite initial observations at +1e155 and -1e155 with invalid floating-point operations configured to raise.
- Ruff 0.15.18 lint/format and git diff --check pass.

This addresses the row reduction, separately from #969's Gaussian normalization coefficients. Overflow of an unrepresentably large squared distance can still produce infinity, correctly corresponding to log density -inf. Arbitrary invalid inputs or an undefined -inf-minus--inf likelihood ratio are not repaired by this change. No optimization-speed or general convergence claim is made.
